properties.name: A coupling with no declared contract is NAMED as a finding, in any project — the seams ratio already knows which pairs they are and throws the list away
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-13, reframing what had been treated as a chore: "the step of adding seams for reflow2 needs to be something reflow2 does for ANY project."

He is right that it was framed wrongly. The prior plan was to hand-label reflow2's own 73 couplings, which fixes one design and teaches reflow2 nothing. Every consumer arrives in the same state — components that depend on each other with no contract recorded between them — and the tool should meet them there.

⭐ THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AND IS DISCARDED. `crates/reflow2-core/src/maturity.rs:203` computes exactly two sets to produce the `seams` band: `couplings` (Component pairs joined by DEPENDS_ON) and `declared` (pairs joined by a real contract — counted only when BOTH a PROVIDES and a CONSUMES are recorded on the same Interface, because "one-sided is exactly the unrecorded contract the capture skill warns about"). It divides one by the other, reports a ratio, and drops the difference on the floor.

`couplings - declared` IS the answer, computed on every maturity run, for every design, and never named. On reflow2's own graph that set has 73 members and the band reads 0%.

🛑 AND NOTHING ELSE COVERS IT. `grep seam` in detect.rs returns nothing: there is no gap source for "these two components are coupled and no contract is declared between them." The two interface detectors run the OPPOSITE direction — `unprovided_interface` (an Interface nobody provides) and `unconsumed_interface` (an Interface nobody consumes) — and both require an Interface to already exist. A design that has never declared one is invisible to both.

WHAT THIS MUST NOT DO, and it is the whole constraint. reflow2 can see THAT two components are coupled. It cannot know WHAT the contract is — the medium, the payload, the auth, the direction. Proposing one would be `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` exactly, and `cap:no-fabricated-repair` is the built answer to that class. So the finding names the PAIR and asks; it never drafts the Interface.

THE SHAPE THAT FOLLOWS FROM THE ABOVE: report each undeclared coupling as a gap whose question is answerable by the person who owns the two components — "cmp:A depends on cmp:B and no contract is recorded between them; is there one, and what is it?" — routed through the ordinary detect→ask path, with `gap_to_prompt` doing the wording.

⚠️ TWO THINGS TO GET RIGHT, both learned from detectors this project has already had to retune:
  · VOLUME. reflow2 alone would emit 73. `chg:gap-reporting-at-corpus-scale` records the same shape biting at an order of magnitude ("300 captured ideas produce 300 identical gaps"), and `unexpected_coupling` was RETIRED for firing on correct architecture. An aggregate keyed on the rule — the shape `cap:aggregate-gap-keying` exists for — is more likely right than 73 individual nags.
  · A DESIGN WITH NO COMPONENT DEPENDENCIES HAS NO SEAMS TO DECLARE, and maturity.rs already says so: "no two Components depend on each other, so there is no seam to declare." The finding must stay silent there rather than reporting a clean 0 as a fault.

📌 WHY IT IS WORTH BUILDING RATHER THAN LABELLING BY HAND: the seams band is reflow2's own frontier and has never moved. Every piece of federation machinery — pair_designs, cap:seam-incompatibility, cap:complementary-pairing, export_surface — is built and verified against fixtures, and has almost nothing to run on in any real design, because no real design has been given a reason to declare its boundaries.
